short_description: Unable to dispense on Standalone app on PC HIS531333
description:
Have tested the standalone software on HIS531333. Able to login successfully using non-AD login, and can search for patient and select a medication. However, after clicking 'Dispense' button, we are unable to dispense a label. Dispensing label section is greyed out and it says 'Unable to connect'.

Our IT team have been looking at the Sophos to see if it is blocking anything, as this was a fix previously. They have found that something specific is blocking the dispensing part of EPMA. 
They have said: "it looks like EPMA tries to load up a different website which is causing it to be blocked. I've tried checking the logs and what it's doing but I can't seem to find the exact website/webpage it's trying to load when you're trying to dispense a label." Please could you help with this issue, and provide the details of what is being opened so that it can be unblocked?
assignment_group: Acute Care Medicines Management Level 1 Team
close_notes:
Hello Hannah,
 
I'm pleased to let you know that we've found a resolution for your case CS1617989.
 
I apologise, I couldn't connect the standalone as I was off last Thursday

The "unable to connect" issue is typically related to antivirus blocking. Since this is a standalone setup, it doesn't connect to any web page or website; instead, it accesses the local folder C:\Ascribe and retrieves DB values from the local database.

Please ensure the following steps are taken:

Antivirus Exclusions: Confirm that the necessary exclusions are in place. I've attached an exclusions list—ask IT to verify that these are correctly configured.
Trusted Sites: Make sure the standalone URL is added to the trusted sites list in Edge/Internet Explorer.
If the issue persists:

Disable Sophos Temporarily: Ask IT to disable Sophos completely and then launch the application. Check if dispensing works without any issues.
Adjust Sophos Settings: If it works after disabling Sophos, request IT to disable the following settings before re-enabling Sophos:
Scan downloads in progress – Disabled
Block access to malicious websites – Disabled
Detect low-reputation files – Disabled
 
We're confident this will fully address the issue. However, if you find that the problem persists, simply click the red 'Reject Solution' button and we'll be happy to investigate further.
 
Kind regards,
Muhammed Rashik

Hello Sue,

Thank you for the updated logs, these contain useful information.

Checking the audit log, you have multiple PCs starting up as comms. Unless you have barcode scanning enabled (unlikely as your comms log shows it disabled on computer L1827) you would need to disable comms on all but one of the following hosts:

[cid:image009.png@01DC7BDC.B1172D60]

Multiple comms will cause file locks with permission errors and other erratic behaviour. We can see evidence of this in your comms log with errors like 'Transaction no longer available' and 'Failed to save Transaction object' when trying to export invoices:

[cid:image010.png@01DC7BDC.B1172D60]

That is a non-standard configuration - PowerGate was not designed to have multiple comms PCs waking up to transact simultaneously.

This is likely the root cause of the issues you are seeing. Each PowerGate with comms enabled that either wakes up on a timer in minutes (interval) or manually by a user clicking the check local button (forced) will take over the import / export process. If another PowerGate does this at the same time, you will have conflicts.

PowerGate is designed to only have one instance with comms enabled waking up automatically (interval). Having so many comms enabled PowerGate PCs though, each with their own unique comms log, makes troubleshooting very difficult and hence is not a supported configuration.

If you want to try and make one PC the main comms enabled PowerGate server and turn the comms off on the others, this is something we can assist with (see attached guide).

Once you have ensured that you only have communications enabled on a single PowerGate PC, if the issue persists we can then continue to investigate the new instances to see if there are other problems.

Failure Message:
pReport_Update_rAMMPrescription [SQLSTATE 01000] (Message 0)  Transaction (Process ID 178) was deadlocked on lock resources with another process and has been chosen as the deadlock victim. Rerun the transaction. [SQLSTATE 40001] (Error 1205).  The step failed.

assignment_group: Acute Care Medicines Management Level 1 Team
close_notes:
Hi Kyle ,

I am pleased to update we have found/come to a resolution for your case CS1739846.

I have verified that all the jobs are running smoothly as anticipated with no failed jobs detected today. 

This deadlocked  issue happens when multiple transactions are interdependent, each waiting for the other to release resources, resulting in a circular dependency that halts their progress. This situation typically arises when one transaction locks a resource that another transaction requires, leading to a complete standstill. For instance, if Transaction A secures a resource while waiting for another, and Transaction B simultaneously locks that same resource while waiting for Transaction A, both transactions become blocked until one of them releases its lock.

We are confident that this will resolve your issue, but if you find that this is not the case, please use the red 'Reject Solution' button so we are able to further investigate this issue for you.
